name: gradient
summary: A linear, radial or conic gradient as background-image, plain or repeating, with an optional colour interpolation space. Written beside linear-gradient and radial-gradient for comparison.

arguments.name: $colors
accepts: one or more colour stops: a colour, or a colour with one or two positions, such as (red 0 10%) (blue 10% 100%)
a position on its own between two colours, as a hint
for a conic gradient the positions are angles or percentages, not lengths
var() for a stop or the whole list
a single colour warns, because browsers before Chrome 135, Firefox 136 and Safari 18.4 drop that gradient

arguments.name: $type
accepts: linear, the default
radial
conic

arguments.name: $direction
accepts: linear only
a direction name such as top or bottom-left
an angle in deg, grad, rad or turn, or 0
"to top" or "to left top" as a string
var() or calc()

arguments.name: $shape
accepts: radial only
circle or ellipse, with an optional size as a string, such as "circle 10px"

arguments.name: $position
accepts: radial or conic
a position name such as center or top-left
at followed by a position, as a string, such as "at 30% 40%"; a radial gradient may put a size before it

arguments.name: $from
accepts: conic only
an angle in deg, grad, rad or turn, 0, or var()

arguments.name: $in
accepts: a colour space: srgb, srgb-linear, display-p3, display-p3-linear, a98-rgb, prophoto-rgb, rec2020, lab, oklab, xyz, xyz-d50 or xyz-d65
a polar space, hsl, hwb, lch or oklch, with an optional hue method as a string, such as "oklch longer hue"
var()
the gradient is written once without the space first, for a browser that does not know it

arguments.name: $repeating
accepts: false, the default
true, for a repeating gradient
